title: On a Möbius double sum
summary: We study the double sum $S_\varepsilon(X)$$=$$\sum_{\substack{d,e\le X}}\frac{μ(d)μ(e)}{[d,e]^{1+\varepsilon}}$, which converges even in the case $\varepsilon=0$, where $μ$ denotes the Möbius function and $[d,e]$ is the least common multiple of $d$ and $e$. Such expressions arise naturally in analytic number theory, notably as the diagonal contribution in certain squared mean values, and they play a significant role in zero-density estimates for the Riemann zeta function and related $L$-functions.
